Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day, face-to-face GP appointment for full cardiorespiratory examination (auscultation of lungs), blood pressure, temperature and repeat pulse check.  
2. If examination consistent with chest infection, commence appropriate oral antibiotic (agent, dose and duration to be decided after review).  
3. Provide patient with practice support team phone number to book the in-person review today.  
4. Safety-net advice: attend ED/call emergency services if breathlessness, chest pain or haemoptysis worsens, if high fever develops, or if she feels generally more unwell.  
5. Discussed very low likelihood of lung cancer given acute presentation; consider follow-up chest X-ray if symptoms persist after treatment.  
6. Current regular medication (methotrexate) unchanged; no new prescriptions issued today.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath and sharp right-sided back pain on deep inspiration since this morning.  
• Associated symptoms: Cough productive of small amounts of blood on two occasions, subjective slight fever, awareness of heartbeat, two-week history of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.  
• No recent long-haul travel, leg pain/swelling, or known personal/family history of thrombosis.  
• Past medical history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).  
• Medications: Methotrexate (dose/route/frequency not documented); last dose taken this morning.  
• Allergies: No known drug or other allergies.  
• Social history: 45-year-old woman; non-smoker; office desk job; lives alone in a flat; owns one cat.

Objective:
• Video examination:  
  – Radial pulse counted 66–74 bpm, regular.  
  – Capillary refill ≤2 s (normal).  
  – Oropharynx unremarkable.  
  – Patient able to speak in full sentences, appears clinically stable.  
  – No palpable cervical lymphadenopathy on self-examination.  
• Blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and temperature: not measured remotely.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute pleuritic chest/back pain with breathlessness and haemoptysis  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia / chest infection (DDx: “Community-acquired pneumonia” – High).  
   - Differential diagnosis:  
     • Pulmonary embolism (DDx – Medium): pleuritic pain/haemoptysis, SLE risk; opposing—normal pulse, no travel/DVT history.  
     • Methotrexate-induced pneumonitis or alveolar haemorrhage (DDx – Medium-Low): on methotrexate; onset unusually abrupt.  
     • SLE-related pleuritis or lupus pneumonitis (DDx – Low).  
     • Primary lung cancer (DDx – Low): acute onset argues against.  
   - Investigations planned: Same-day physical examination incl. auscultation, BP, temp; possible chest X-ray if not improving.  
   - Treatment planned: Empirical oral antibiotic if examination supports infection; hold off prescribing until after in-person review.  
   - Relevant referrals: Same-day GP clinic appointment arranged.

2. Anxiety regarding possible lung cancer  
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Health anxiety; lung cancer considered unlikely at present.  
   - Differential diagnosis: Primary lung cancer (DDx – Low).  
   - Investigations planned: Chest X-ray if persistent or worsening symptoms after initial management.  
   - Treatment planned: Reassurance provided; safety-net advice given.  
   - Relevant referrals: None at this stage.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Objective vitals (BP, RR, SpO₂, temperature), full medication list with doses, recent SLE/methotrexate monitoring bloods.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially gave name “Tracy Chapman,” later answered to “Doris” when physician asked (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor overlaps and name inconsistency as above.
